answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer, any delivery disruption is costly, so switching primary supply to an unproven-at-this-scale low-cost vendor (memory_c2) carries risk that a single prior positive onboarding experience doesn't fully retire—especially since c2 doesn't speak to sustained volume reliability under tight capacity. Memory_c4 and c6 suggest the incumbent has previously conceded on price/terms and multi-year volume pricing without narrowing scope, and c1 shows the incumbent relationship has been stable across cycles. Given the 14-day window, the safest path to hit the 18% mandate without raising delivery risk is to aggressively renegotiate with the incumbent using the low-cost quote as leverage, rather than committing the single available sourcing action this cycle to a full vendor switch. I want to verify the actual archived records for c4 (negotiation outcome specifics) and c2 (switch outcome specifics, especially any mention of ramp risk or volume limits) before finalizing, since the consolidated summaries may understate risk relevant to a zero-buffer line.
